年の割に 'for one's age' is read としのわりに; ねん never carries the 'age' sense (only counting/compounds). Apply the parallel romaji fix: ...toshinowariniwa...

notes: 'Keep thinking' = continuative (考え続ける), wrong aspect for ておく; contradicts the sentence's own expl_en and とく gloss. lit fields must mirror structure, so this is semantic, not stylistic.
'keep thinking' is continuative, wrong aspect for 〜ておく (do-and-leave-settled); contradicts the token gloss, expl, and the correct lit_pt mirror. Suggested fix is sound.

findings.issue: Wrong grammar claim: the sentence is 車が + いっぱい + でした (quantity predicate + polite past copula). It is NOT the 〜でいっぱい 'full of' pattern — that requires で before いっぱい (車でいっぱい). Learner may misparse でした's で as part of でいっぱい.
findings.current: Here いっぱい functions as a noun predicate with the sense of 'full/packed,' in the pattern 〜でいっぱい ('full of').
findings.suggested: いっぱい here is a quantity predicate ('a lot'): 車が + いっぱい + でした (polite past copula); NOT the 〜でいっぱい pattern, which requires で (車でいっぱい).
findings.fix: いっぱい here is a quantity predicate ('a lot'): 車が + いっぱい + でした (polite past copula); NOT the 〜でいっぱい pattern, which requires で (車でいっぱい).
notes: Sentence has が, not で: 車がいっぱいでした is quantity predicate + past copula; claiming the 〜でいっぱい pattern is a false parse (that requires 車でいっぱい).
で in でした is the past copula, not a particle before いっぱい; sentence is 車が+いっぱい+でした. Claiming the 〜でいっぱい pattern teaches a false parse.

findings.issue: Same wrong grammar claim as expl_en: asserts the sentence instantiates o padrão 〜でいっぱい, but there is no で before いっぱい here; でした is the polite past copula. Teaches a false parse.

findings.fix: いっぱい aqui é predicado de quantidade ('um monte'): 車が + いっぱい + でした (passado polido); NÃO é o padrão 〜でいっぱい, que exige で (車でいっぱい).
notes: Same false pattern claim in pt: no で before いっぱい; でした is the polite past copula, so 'no padrão 〜でいっぱい' teaches a wrong structure.
Same false 〜でいっぱい claim in pt: no particle で precedes いっぱい. Real parse: quantity predicate + polite past copula でした.

findings.fix: せ = base do auxiliar causativo せる sobre さ- (未然形 de する) → させ; sem contração / same in en, no 'ささせ'
notes: させる = さ (mizenkei of する) + せる; 'ささせ... contracted to させ' is invented morphology. Parallel note in tatoeba-118746 has the correct analysis.
させる = さ (mizenkei of する) + せる; 'ささせ→させ contraction' is an invented form. Parallel note in sent:tatoeba-118746 gives the correct analysis.

かも(しれない) expresses possibility ('might'), not likelihood ('probably'); en, lit_pt ('talvez') and both expls say maybe — lit_en is the outlier.

Standard reading of 何 before が is なに (なにが); なん only before だ/で/と/の and counters. なんが teaches a wrong pronunciation.

findings.issue: 私の姉は is the topic/subject 'my older sister', but lit_pt renders it as a possessive 'da minha irmã-mais-velha' ('of my older sister'), misrepresenting the structure; lit_en correctly treats her as the one working.

findings.issue: Garbled parenthetical: '(もする = 'fazer')' presents もする as one unit meaning 'fazer'; the English version has '(with する = 'to do')', so the pt should read '(com する = 'fazer')'.

expl_pt '(もする = \'fazer\')' misglosses もする as 'fazer' (する alone = fazer); expl_en has '(with する = \'to do\')', so pt dropped 'com'. Suggested '(com する = \'fazer\')' restores parity.

findings.issue: In 電話くれれば, くれる is the main (and only) verb of the clause, 'give (me) a call' with を dropped — not an auxiliary attached to a て-form. Labeling it 'verbo auxiliar' contradicts the corpus role convention (cf. み in 聞いてみた) and the item's own explanation.

findings.suggested: verbo principal (benefactivo: dar/fazer para o falante)
findings.fix: verbo principal (benefactivo: dar/fazer para o falante)
notes: 電話（を）くれれば has no て-form; くれる is the clause's main verb. Corpus convention elsewhere tags noun/を+くれる/あげる as 'verbo principal' (て+X = auxiliar); this item is the lone outlier and contradicts its own expl_pt ('O verbo くれる').
電話(を)くれれば: くれる is the main transitive verb, not a 補助動詞 (no て-form). The item itself tags 電話 as 'objeto', so 'verbo auxiliar' self-contradicts.

findings.issue: Mangled punctuation at the end: closing quote and period are inside the parenthesis — "(quem é?'.)" — leaving the quote opened before 'aquele' unclosed properly.

findings.suggested: destacar a informação buscada: 'aquele que inventou o telefone' (quem é?).
findings.fix: A frase usa a construção de foco 「〜のは〜だ」: 「電話を発明した」 (inventou o telefone) é nominalizado por 「の」 e marcado por 「は」 como o tema já conhecido, e a parte nova/focalizada é 「だれ」 (quem), fechada por 「ですか」. Essa estrutura serve para destacar a informação buscada: 'aquele que inventou o telefone' (quem é?).
notes: Genuine typographic defect: "(quem é?'.)" misplaces the closing quote and period inside the parenthesis, leaving the quote opened at 'aquele' badly closed and the sentence without a final period.
Punctuation is genuinely mangled: "(quem é?'.)" closes the quote and period inside the parenthesis; proposed fix is correct.

findings.issue: In the parenthetical gloss, 'tomara que logo virem' is ungrammatical: after 'tomara que' the verb needs present subjunctive ('venham'/'cheguem'); 'virem' is the personal infinitive of 'vir' (or 3pl of 'virar', which cannot take 'férias' as subject).
findings.current: Ah, cedo férias-de-verão em não-vira, será? (= tomara que logo virem)

'tomara que logo virem' has no valid pt-BR reading here (reads as 'ver' fut. subj.; 'virar' 3pl clashes with the impersonal なる) and contradicts expl_pt's 'chegue logo'.

findings.issue: ３０分 is transcribed さんれいふん (digit-by-digit 'san-rei fun'). No native reading: 30分 is さんじゅっぷん (or さんじっぷん), with ぷん after the geminate.

さんれいふん is a digit-by-digit misreading; ３０分 as a duration is only さんじゅっぷん/さんじっぷん. れい-readings apply to codes/phone numbers, never 'every 30 minutes'.

findings.issue: 'bati-carteira' is not a Portuguese word — verb+noun compounds use third-person 'bate-' (cf. bate-papo), and 'levar um bati-carteira' is unidiomatic BP. Use the normal colloquial phrasing for being pickpocketed.

'bati-carteira' is malformed (compounds use bate-, cf. bate-papo); even 'bate-carteira' names the agent, not the event. 'Bateram minha carteira no trem' is idiomatic BP at the right register.

findings.issue: Tense concordance error: future subjunctive 'estiver' paired with conditional 'iria' is ungrammatical in pt-BR. The JP のだが expresses counterfactual regret (we would go, but the weather is not good), requiring imperfect subjunctive + conditional.

notes: 'estiver'+'iria' is a real concordance error; のだが (and the batch's own en/expl) is counterfactual, so 'estivesse... iria' is required.
Mixed 'estiver'+'iria' breaks pt-BR tense concordance; JP のだが is counterfactual regret (own expl says 'iríamos, mas o tempo não está bom'), requiring 'estivesse…iria'.

findings.issue: Note (both languages) calls 入っ a 'voiced' (sonorizada/voiced) connective stem. 入った is 促音便 (gemination, small っ); nothing is voiced (contrast 読んだ, where the ending voices to だ).

入った is 促音便 (gemination); nothing voices (contrast 読んだ→だ). 'Sonorizada/voiced' teaches a false rule. Mirror the fix in the en note ('geminate connective stem (促音便)').

findings.issue: Literal mirror conveys a wrong meaning: たった今、行ったところよ = '(he) has just gone this very moment'. 'Well now, that was it, you see' misreads both たった今 and 〜たところ and teaches a false structure.
findings.current: Well now, that was it, you see.
findings.suggested: Just now — (he) is right at the point of having gone, you know.
findings.fix: Just now — (he) is right at the point of having gone, you know.
notes: 'Well now, that was it, you see' mirrors nothing of たった今、行ったところよ; even deliberately-literal fields must track the actual structure (just-completed 〜たところ).
'Well now, that was it' contains no motion verb and misreads both たった今 ('just now', not an interjection) and 〜たところ (just-completed); it mirrors a structure the sentence does not have.

findings.issue: 'Bem-agora, foi-ponto, viu.' is unintelligible in Portuguese and drops the 〜たところ 'acabou de' (just-completed) meaning the field should mirror.

'foi-ponto' is uninterpretable Portuguese and the field drops the just-completed 〜たところ meaning; deliberate literalness still requires intelligible mirroring.

findings.issue: Note claims 行っ is い-onbin of 行く. False: 行く is the classic exception that takes 促音便 (行って/行った), not い音便 (*行いた). Teaches a wrong conjugation rule; the en note repeats the error.
findings.current: forma 音便 (い-onbin) de 行く, base para o passado た → 行った
findings.suggested: forma 音便 (促音便, com っ — exceção de 行く) , base para o passado た → 行った
findings.fix: pt-BR: "forma 音便 (促音便, com っ — 行く é exceção, não usa い-onbin), base para o passado た → 行った"; en: "音便 form (促音便 with っ — 行く is the exception, not い-onbin), base for the past た → 行った" (also fixes the stray space before the comma in the proposed text).
notes: 行く is the standard 促音便 exception (行った, never *行いた); 'い-onbin' teaches a false rule and the en note repeats it.
行く is the classic 促音便 exception (行って/行った), never い-onbin (*行いた); the token itself is 行っ with っ. Fix the en note identically. Suggested fix had a typo — cleaned version supplied.

findings.issue: Mirror misparses genitive 庭の ('the garden's', noun-linking の) as a locative adjunct 'In the garden,', contradicting the expl, which correctly teaches の as possession; lit_pt keeps the genitive.
findings.current: In the garden, the roses are blooming.
findings.suggested: The garden's roses are blooming.

notes: 庭の is adnominal genitive; 'In the garden,' reads as 庭で and contradicts the expl's own の-as-possession teaching, while lit_pt keeps the genitive. Minor but real.
lit fields exist to mirror structure: 庭の is a noun-linking genitive, and 'In the garden,' recasts it as a locative adjunct, contradicting both the expl (possession/origin) and lit_pt ('Do jardim').

鳥 is the nominal predicate of だったら; the hypothesis' implied subject is 'eu'. Calling the same token 'predicado nominal' and 'sujeito' is self-contradictory in a grammar-role field.

findings.issue: 何時 must be read なんじ here: the sentence asks a clock time with に (en: 'What time...?', pt: 'A que horas...?'). いつ ('when') does not take に in this scheduling sense; なんじに is the standard reading.

findings.fix: ちょうしょくわなんじにいたしますか。

何時に asking a clock time (en 'What time', pt 'A que horas') reads なんじ; いつ would need 'when'. Kana teaches a wrong in-context reading.

Current PT parses as 'the match that ended lasted long', inverting main vs relative clause; the literal mirror shows the wrong structure.

findings.issue: Literal inverts the 〜ていく structure: 試していく is try(-te) + いく (continuation onward), but 'Go and try (it)' reads as motion-then-action (= 行って試す) and as an imperative, not a first-person statement.

findings.fix: The core is やってくる, a lexicalized compound verb 'to come along / to turn up': the て-form of やる plus the auxiliary くる, where 〜てくる adds movement approaching the speaker/present ('comes arriving').

findings.issue: Misparse: ここまでにする is ここまで (limit particle まで 'up to') + にする ('settle on'), parallel to おしまいにする in this same family; it is not the compound deadline particle までに ('by X'). The item's own tokens split まで|に. Calling までに the unit that 'marks the limit point' teaches a false particle function and invites まで/までに confusion.
findings.current: The sentence uses 「ここまでに(する)」, where the target までに marks the limit point 'up to here'
findings.suggested: The sentence uses ここまで + にする: まで marks the limit 'up to here', and にする ('settle on/wrap up') closes it — parallel to おしまいにする.
findings.fix: The sentence uses ここまで + にする: まで marks the limit 'up to here' and にする ('to settle on / make it be') wraps it up, so 「ここまでにする」 = 'to make it stop at this point, to call it here' — parallel to おしまいにする and このくらいにする. 「今日は」 is the topic ('as for today'). The verb する appears with 「ておく」 ('to do in advance / to leave done') in the volitional form 「おこう」 ('let's...'). Note this is not the compound particle までに ('by [a deadline]'): here まで and に belong to different pieces.
notes: Real misparse: ここまで+にする, not compound までに (deadline). Contradicts its own まで|に token split and sibling 171787/171792 expls. Fix must also drop the closing までに sentence.

ここまでにする is ここまで + にする (parallel to おしまいにする/このくらいにする in this same batch); calling までに the unit contradicts the item's own まで|に token split and the corpus's other までに explanations, which correctly define it as the deadline compound.

findings.issue: Same misparse as expl_en: the structure is ここまで + にする, not the compound particle までに ('by X'). The unit analysis contradicts the token split まで|に and the parallel にする sentences in this family (おしまいにする, このくらいにする).

findings.suggested: A frase usa ここまで + にする: まで marca o limite 'até aqui', e にする ('decidir/encerrar em') fecha a frase — paralelo a おしまいにする.
findings.fix: A frase usa ここまで + にする: まで marca o limite 'até aqui' e にする ('decidir por / deixar em') encerra a ação, ou seja, 「ここまでにする」 = 'fazer parar neste ponto, encerrar aqui' — paralelo a おしまいにする e このくらいにする. 「今日は」 é o tópico ('quanto a hoje'). O verbo する aparece com 「ておく」 (fazer algo de antemão / deixar feito) na forma volitiva 「おこう」 ('vamos...'). Atenção: não se trata da partícula composta までに ('até [um prazo]'); aqui まで e に pertencem a blocos diferentes.
notes: Mesmo defeito real: ここまで+にする, não a partícula composta までに. A correção precisa cobrir também a frase final que repete 'までに define o limite'.
Mesmo erro de análise do expl_en: o に pertence a にする, não ao composto までに de prazo; a explicação contradiz a segmentação まで|に do próprio item.
